issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping, failure or stuck in one gear
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, or the van staying in second or third gear (limp mode) with weak acceleration.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic used in these minivans has a long record of clutch, solenoid and internal wear problems, and it is sensitive to using the wrong fluid.
issues.next: Have codes read and the fluid level and type checked right away; use only the manufacturer's specified fluid. Slipping that keeps getting worse usually means a rebuild.

issues.t: Fuel leak from fuel rail O-rings
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell under the hood or fuel wetness around the top of the engine.
issues.why: The rubber O-rings on the under-hood fuel rail can break down with age and let fuel seep out, which creates a fire risk. Chrysler recalled these vans to add a seal.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 00V268. If you smell fuel under the hood, don't drive it; have it towed and inspected.

issues.t: Fuel leak where the fuel pump mounts to the tank
issues.sym: Fuel smell around the rear of the van or drips from the top of the fuel tank, especially after a fill-up.
issues.why: The nut that holds the fuel pump module in the tank could allow fuel to leak past its seal. Chrysler recalled these vans to replace the nut and O-ring.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 99V216. Don't park in a garage or keep driving if you smell fuel; have it inspected promptly.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bolt can break
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, wandering steering, or the front wheel shifting out of position.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the front lower control arm to the crossmember could fracture, letting the arm separate and causing a loss of control. Chrysler recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 01V152. If you hear front-end clunks or the steering feels loose, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Radio short circuit can start a speaker fire
issues.sym: A burning plastic or electrical smell, crackling speakers, or smoke from a speaker area.
issues.why: A short circuit in the radio could overheat a speaker and start a fire. Chrysler recalled affected vans.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 04V531. If you smell burning electrical parts, turn the van off and have it inspected before driving again.

issues.t: Fuel tank control valve weld can leak
issues.sym: Gasoline smell near the rear of the van or fuel wetness on top of the tank.
issues.why: A weld on a valve in the fuel tank could separate and let fuel leak, creating a fire risk. Chrysler recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 02V274. If you smell fuel, don't drive it; have it inspected.

issues.t: Power steering cooler hose can split
issues.sym: Power steering fluid on the ground, a whining pump, heavier steering, or a burning smell if fluid hits hot parts.
issues.why: The upper power steering cooler hose could split and spray fluid in the engine bay, which can cause a fire. Chrysler recalled these vans. Power steering whine is also a common complaint on this generation.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check the VIN for recall 04V386. If you see fluid leaking or smell burning, stop driving and have it repaired.

issues.t: Power liftgate latch may not lock
issues.sym: A liftgate-ajar warning, or the liftgate opening on its own while driving.
issues.why: The power liftgate latch might not fully engage when closed. Chrysler recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 05V134. Make sure the liftgate is fully latched before driving and don't carry loose cargo at the back until it's fixed.

issues.t: Front passenger seat belt retractor may be assembled wrong
issues.sym: The passenger seat belt may not lock or retract normally.
issues.why: Some right front seat belt retractors on vans without Stow 'n Go seating were not assembled correctly and may not hold in a crash. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 04V047 and have it fixed before carrying a front passenger.

issues.t: Harsh shifting, slipping or limp mode from the six-speed automatic
issues.sym: Hard or delayed shifts, slipping, jerking, whining, slow engagement into gear, or being stuck in a single gear.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic draws many complaints for shift quality, solenoid and electronic faults that trigger limp mode, and internal wear.
issues.next: Have trouble codes read and the fluid checked soon. Ask a dealer about software updates; solenoid faults are often repairable without a full rebuild.

issues.t: Transmission pump can seize and cause loss of drive
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power to the wheels, warning lights, or the van not moving in gear.
issues.why: The transmission oil pump on some vans built from mid-2015 to spring 2016 could seize, so the transmission loses hydraulic pressure. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V461. If the van loses drive, get to a safe spot and have it towed.

issues.t: Integrated power module (TIPM) failure
issues.sym: No-start, stalling in traffic, a fuel pump that keeps running, wipers or horn acting on their own, or overnight battery drain.
issues.why: The under-hood power module that runs many relays and circuits, including the fuel pump relay, can fail internally.
issues.next: Have the module diagnosed before replacing starters, fuel pumps or batteries. Stalling is a safety risk, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Ignition key can slip out of Run and shut off the engine
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, often after the key is bumped or a heavy key ring swings, with loss of power steering and brake assist.
issues.why: The ignition switch could move out of the Run position, cutting the engine and disabling the air bags. Chrysler recalled these vans, expanding an earlier recall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recalls 14V373 and 11V139. Until fixed, remove extra weight from the key ring.

issues.t: A/C water can drip on the air bag module
issues.sym: Air bag warning light, and in rare cases air bags going off without a crash.
issues.why: Condensation from the heating and A/C system could leak onto the air bag control module. Chrysler recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 11V394 and get it fixed promptly.

issues.t: Air bag control unit can corrode and fail
issues.sym: Air bag warning light on the dash; air bags might not deploy in a crash or could deploy unexpectedly.
issues.why: The air bag control unit could corrode internally. Chrysler recalled affected vans to replace it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V047 and have it done as soon as possible.

issues.t: Steering wheel emblem can break loose in an air bag deployment
issues.sym: No warning signs; the risk only appears if the driver air bag goes off.
issues.why: The emblem on the steering wheel air bag cover, or its nuts, could come loose and fly toward the driver when the air bag deploys. Chrysler recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V396 and get the cover replaced promptly.

issues.t: Driver door vent window switch can overheat
issues.sym: A burning smell, melted plastic or smoke near the driver's door armrest, or a vent window switch that stops working.
issues.why: The switch for the rear vent windows in the driver's armrest could overheat, especially if liquids got into it, and start a fire. Chrysler recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 14V234. If you smell burning near the door, park and have it inspected before driving again.

issues.t: Steering column rivet may be missing
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs; in some cases the steering wheel may feel loose.
issues.why: A pivot rivet in the steering column could be missing or installed wrong, weakening the column in a frontal crash. Chrysler recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 11V315 and have the column inspected.

issues.t: Misfires from a failing left cylinder head
issues.sym: Check engine light with misfire codes on the driver-side bank, a rough idle and ticking.
issues.why: The left cylinder head on early 3.6L engines can develop valve seat wear or cracks and lose compression. Chrysler extended warranty coverage on the left head to 10 years or 150,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether your VIN is covered by the cylinder head warranty extension before paying for repairs.

issues.t: Ticking engine from worn rocker arms
issues.sym: A ticking noise from the top of the engine, then misfires, a check engine light and loss of power.
issues.why: Rocker arms and valvetrain parts in the 3.6L can wear early and shift out of place. Chrysler told dealers to fit redesigned rocker arms, and owners filed a lawsuit over the problem.
issues.next: Have ticking diagnosed early, before it causes misfires or valve damage. Keep oil changes on time with the correct oil.

issues.t: Debris in the engine can ruin rod bearings
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, low oil pressure warning, or the engine seizing.
issues.why: Some engines built in late summer 2011 had debris left in the block that could damage the connecting rod bearings. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 11V487. If you hear knocking, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Right rear wheel hub may not be fully machined
issues.sym: Grinding, humming or a wobbling right rear wheel.
issues.why: Some right rear hub and bearing units on vans built in November 2011 were not fully machined and could allow the wheel to separate. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 12V141. If a rear wheel feels loose or noisy, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Air bag software can deploy the wrong air bags
issues.sym: Possible air bag warning light; otherwise no warning signs.
issues.why: Software errors in the air bag control module on some 2013 vans could deploy air bags on the wrong side in a crash or keep them from working properly. Chrysler issued two recalls.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 13V283 and 13V291 and get the software update.

issues.t: Tire pressure monitor may not warn of low tires
issues.sym: Tire pressure light doesn't come on, or shows the wrong tire, even when a tire is low.
issues.why: Software on vans built in spring 2014 could fail to learn where each sensor is mounted. Chrysler recalled them for a reprogram.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 14V632 and check tire pressures by hand until it's done.

issues.t: Blind spot monitoring stops working
issues.sym: Blind spot warning lights that stay off, give false alerts, or show a system fault message.
issues.why: The rear blind spot sensors on upper trims can fail.
issues.next: Have the sensors checked. Until repaired, rely on mirrors and shoulder checks before changing lanes.

issues.t: Steering wheel clockspring can disable the driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light on, and sometimes the horn or the steering wheel buttons stop working.
issues.why: The coiled ribbon of wire that feeds the driver airbag through the steering column can be wound wrong or wear through, breaking the circuit to the bag.
issues.next: Have it checked by VIN and the clockspring replaced. Chrysler covered this under two recall campaigns and extended the warranty on the part, so ask the dealer before paying.

issues.t: Loose trim can jam a rear seat belt (recall)
issues.sym: A rear outboard or third-row belt will not pull out, will not latch, or feels blocked.
issues.why: Interior trim near the rear belts can come loose and fall into the belt assembly, which stops the belt working at all.
issues.next: Do not seat anyone there until it is repaired. The dealer fits foam blockers and inspects or replaces the third-row belts free under the recall.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractor may not restrain properly (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing obvious. The belt looks and feels normal.
issues.why: Front belt retractors built in this period may not meet the federal strength standard, so the belt may not hold an occupant in a crash.
issues.next: Have the van checked by VIN and the retractor replaced. The repair is free under the recall.

issues.t: Built-in child seat harness is hard to release (recall)
issues.sym: The shoulder harness on the integrated child seat sticks and will not pull out or let go easily.
issues.why: Dirt and crumbs build up around the latch plate, and the plate then cannot move the way it needs to for the harness to work.
issues.next: Clean the latch area and have the dealer fit the release extender and clips supplied under the campaign. Use a separate child seat until the harness works freely.

issues.t: Built-in child seat harness routed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing a parent would see. The harness webbing runs on the wrong side of a metal bar inside the seat back.
issues.why: On some vans the integrated child seat webbing was threaded around a reinforcement bar, so the harness cannot hold a child properly in a crash.
issues.next: Use a separate child seat and have the dealer inspect and reroute the webbing. The work is free under the recall.

issues.t: Master cylinder seal can fail and lengthen stopping distance (recall)
issues.sym: Brake warning light on, a pedal that sinks or feels long, and the brake fluid level dropping with no puddle on the ground.
issues.why: The rear seal in the brake master cylinder can leak, letting fluid get pulled into the vacuum booster instead of pushing the brakes.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Treat soft brakes as urgent and have the van towed if the pedal is going to the floor. The dealer replaces the master cylinder free under the recall.

issues.t: Wiper motor shaft can break and stop the wipers (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop partway across the windshield or stop moving at all, often with the motor still humming.
issues.why: The armature shaft inside the front wiper motor can snap, which leaves the blades with nothing driving them.
issues.next: Do not drive in rain or snow until it is fixed. The dealer inspects and replaces the wiper motor free under the recall.

issues.t: Front crash sensors can corrode and disable the airbags (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light stays on, usually on vans driven where roads are salted.
issues.why: The up-front crash sensors can crack and let water in, or corrode at their mounting, so they stop reporting to the airbag computer.
issues.next: Have the sensors replaced with the newer design. Two recall campaigns cover this, and Chrysler also extended coverage on failed sensors, so ask before paying.

issues.t: Power sliding doors quit working
issues.sym: A power door will not open or close from the button, the handle or the key fob, stops part way, or opens by itself. Sometimes it works when the van is cold and not when it is warm.
issues.why: The cables and rollers in the door track wear and fray, and the wiring that runs through the flexible loop into the door breaks where it bends every time the door moves. A worn latch or a failed door module can also stop the motor from running.
issues.next: Have the door track, the cables and the flex harness checked, and keep using the door by hand in the meantime. Get it looked at before a trip, because a door that will not latch is not safe to drive with.

issues.t: Rear air conditioning stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The rear vents blow warm while the front still cools, or nothing cools at all once the refrigerant has escaped. A recharge helps for a while and then the air goes warm again.
issues.why: The rear evaporator and the long lines that feed it sit under the van and corrode, so the refrigerant slowly leaks out. Topping the system up does nothing about the hole it is leaking from.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested with dye or a sniffer before anyone adds refrigerant, so you pay to fix the leak once instead of recharging it every summer. It is a comfort problem, so it can wait until you are ready.
